$comment: Bigfoot skeleton. The clip table is not here — it is assets/manifest.json's rigContract, and the build derives every clip, tick, event and input from it. See art/rig/README.md.
$maneComment: Bigfoot's `mane` hangs off the body, and it is the only species where it does. On the other five the mane is a head ruff; here the layer is a whole-figure fur trim — brow, mantle, chest, and separate islands along both arms — so a head pivot would swing the arm fur off the arms. The cost is the mirror of that: the arm-fur islands do not follow the arms during walk or attack, because the art is one flattened layer and nothing in a rig can un-flatten it. Splitting the trim per limb is an art change, not a rig change.
$paletteComment: The fur trim is the mane, and it is also the signature part, so there is no separate accent: the manifest mint sits on the leaf tucked in the fur, a few dozen pixels inside the same flattened layer. No tint slots ship in this rig — art-pipeline §6.2 carries the measurement that says why, and the property names the client will drive when they do (mane).
$stageComment: The artboard is deliberately LARGER than the art canvas. The 1024 canvas is commissioned with 8px of margin (manifest tolerance.edgeMarginPx), which is enough for a part not to be born against the edge and nowhere near enough for a rig to rotate, leap or topple inside — a knocked-down character needs its own diagonal, and a mythic tier fills the canvas standing still. So the art canvas sits centred in a 1400 stage with 188px of blank on every side, at scale 1, and the standing point still lands on the manifest origin. Rest is still 1:1 with assembled.png inside that sub-rect, which is what build-rigs checks.
